snippets.text: A spacecraft can fly past a planet, fire no engines, and leave faster than it arrived.
snippets.spoken: A spacecraft can fly past a planet, fire no engines, and leave faster than it arrived.

snippets.text: Watch from the planet first. Gravity pulls it in, swings it around, and lets it go.
snippets.spoken: Watch from the planet first. Gravity pulls it in, swings it around, and lets it go.

snippets.text: Measured from the planet, it leaves about as fast as it arrived. Only its direction has changed.
snippets.spoken: Measured from the planet, it leaves about as fast as it arrived. Only its direction has changed.

snippets.text: But the planet is moving around the Sun. Seen from the Sun, that curve is carried along with it, and the spacecraft leaves faster.
snippets.spoken: But the planet is moving around the Sun. Seen from the Sun, that curve is carried along with it, and the spacecraft leaves faster.

snippets.text: The energy isn't free. It's borrowed from the planet's own orbit, by an almost imperceptible amount.
snippets.spoken: The energy isn't free. It's borrowed from the planet's own orbit, by an almost imperceptible amount.

snippets.text: Same flyby. Two answers. Both of them right.
snippets.spoken: Same flyby. Two answers. Both of them right.

snippets.text: Falling into the Sun sounds easy. It isn't.
snippets.spoken: Falling into the Sun sounds easy. It isn't.

snippets.text: Earth is racing sideways around the Sun at about thirty kilometres a second. And so is everything we launch from it.
snippets.spoken: Earth is racing sideways around the Sun at about thirty kilometres a second. And so is everything we launch from it.

snippets.text: Aim straight at the Sun, and that sideways speed carries you right past it.
snippets.spoken: Aim straight at the Sun, and that sideways speed carries you right past it.

snippets.text: NASA's Parker Solar Probe needed to shed about fifty-three thousand miles per hour of it.
snippets.spoken: NASA's Parker Solar Probe needed to shed about fifty-three thousand miles per hour of it.

snippets.text: So it flew past Venus seven times. Together, those flybys reduced its orbital energy around the Sun, and its orbit reached closer in.
snippets.spoken: So it flew past Venus seven times. Together, those flybys reduced its orbital energy around the Sun, and its orbit reached closer in.

snippets.text: Then it fell. On Christmas Eve, twenty twenty-four, it passed closer to the Sun than any spacecraft before it.
snippets.spoken: Then it fell. On Christmas Eve, twenty twenty-four, it passed closer to the Sun than any spacecraft before it.

snippets.text: One spacecraft. Four giant planets. One trip. That only works if the planets are in just the right places.
snippets.spoken: One spacecraft. Four giant planets. One trip. That only works if the planets are in just the right places.

snippets.text: In the late nineteen-seventies, they drifted into a favourable alignment, one that comes around roughly once every hundred and seventy-five years.
snippets.spoken: In the late nineteen-seventies, they drifted into a favourable alignment, one that comes around roughly once every hundred and seventy-five years.

snippets.text: Not a straight line. But it made a journey past all four possible, and Voyager 2 took it.
snippets.spoken: Not a straight line. But it made a journey past all four possible, and Voyager 2 took it.

snippets.text: At Jupiter, gravity bent its path toward Saturn. At Saturn, toward Uranus. At Uranus, toward Neptune, which it reached in nineteen eighty-nine.
snippets.spoken: At Jupiter, gravity bent its path toward Saturn. At Saturn, toward Uranus. At Uranus, toward Neptune, which it reached in nineteen eighty-nine.

snippets.text: Each flyby reshaped its route. Measured from the Sun, together they more than doubled its speed.
